Strengthening Policy, Legal, Regulatory and Institutional Framework to support the Development of a Sustainable Bio Fuel Industry in Tanzania and develop instruments to facilitate the domestic use of bio fuel, to complement the use of bio mass and fossil fuels

The project is basically focused at putting in place Policy, Legal, Regulatory and Institutional Frameworks, however at a bigger picture the project aimed at building the Tanzania biofuels industry. The project is implemented as per the formulated four Project components which include;- i) Component 1: The organizational capacity of the government to coordinate, regulate and support the development of plans and legal instruments relevant to the biofuels industry sector developed. ii) Component 2: Adequate capacity to assess the biofuels industry from a fiscal and financial perspective within the government and among financial institutions developed. iii) Component 3: Policy and legal instruments to support and regulate the development of a sustainable biofuels industry contributing to prioritized development objectives of Tanzania are developed. iv) Component 4: There is public support, participation and awareness regarding the biofuels industry in Tanzania.

Assessing the above mentioned components some results partially achived, if there were good implementation progress the contribution could have contributed to the achievement of the outcome objective of the development intervention. Some of the results achieved since the start of the project include the production/preparation of the draft reports as following;- Produced draft Liquid Bioenergy policy, which later was intergrated in the main Energy Policy of 2015- Developed draft capacity building programme- Initited awareness programme and knowledge to Tanzania Financial Institutions and the community at large.- Produced draft Strategic Environment Assessment (SEA ) report ready for final review- Initiated the drafting of Liquid Bioenergy Legislation.- Produced draft Liquid Bioenergy Strategy ready for stakeholders review -The project enabled to raise awareness to a number of stakeholders to understand the benefit that biofuels can provide, including the use of biofuels as domestic fuel, transport fuel and running multifunctional platform. Few companies started to develop biofuels stove for domestic coking, grinding running sawing machines and generating electricity. Some of these results were used/intergarted during the preparation of the Energy Policy in 2015, as it was decided by the ministry that there should be only one energy policy, but comprising all other sources of energy - being it biofuel, biomass, LPG, solar etc etc, in order to avoide confusion of having several policies for each energy source. The following documents produced/developed by the project and can be accessed at the Ministry of Energy; 1. Draft Liquid Biofuels Policy.2. Draft Liquid Bio-energy Act No. 2015.3. Tanzania Biofuels Policy Framework – REGULATORY FRAMEWORK.4. Strategic Environmental Assessment for National Liquid Bioenergy Policy.5. Major awareness Inception Report.6. Draft Major awareness manual.7. Biofuels Guidelines. Proposed list of unfinished activities supposed to be included in the Energy Sector Capacity strengthening project during the inception phase were as follows below, unfortunately due to the reason beyond control of the Embassy the intervention did not take place:- - Follow-up on Biofuel Strategic Environment Assessment (SEA) approval from the Vice President's Office- Final review of the Biofuel proposition and regulatory framework- Finalization of Biofuel strategy preparation- Finalization of preparation Liquid Bioenergy Legislation.- Conduct Major Biofuel Awareness Campaign- Undertake Biofuels Agro-Ecological Zoning However the Energy Sector Strengthening Project did not take place due to reason beyond embassy control. The embassy in consultation with Embassy Norway have decised not to start that project.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
